fact: The municipal revenue management system GRB 2.0 was one of four digital solutions developed by the GIZ-run REMO project in partnership with the Ministry of the Interior (1 May 2022 to 30 April 2026).
GRB 2.0 came out of REMO, a bilateral Germany-Tunisia cooperation programme carried out by GIZ over four years; the article gives no domestic funding line.

The webinar synthesis (2024) describes a cooperation project in Bizerte (about 140,000 inhabitants) to develop three services, among them electronic payment of municipal fees and GRB 2.0 to digitalise the commune's budget resource management processes; it says online payment was not used by citizens, and names no other commune.

The GIZ study (March 2022) says that for the TCL business tax the commune president draws up a document listing the taxable persons and amounts due, enters it in the commune's GRB system and transmits it to the regional treasurer and the municipal receiver, who follow collection on the GRB network.
The GRB entry made by the commune is visible on the GRB network to the regional treasurer and the municipal receiver of the Ministry of Finance, who follow collection.
The study describes the GRB system as the communes' system and recommends adapting it to hold more types of municipal revenue and digital payment, but gives no count or share of communes using it.

For ceremony authorisation fees, the study describes payment to the commune's cash-collection office (régie de recettes) against a receipt taken from a stub book (journal à souches) where no other proof of payment is used.
Ceremony fees paid to the commune's cash-collection office are receipted from a paper stub book, with cash paid in to the municipal receiver against a deposit slip.
